## 🚨 Read this before scheduling it: the report ranked this FIRST, and the measurement says otherwise
The report called classification "the headline finding — the only candidate that removes a category of manual work rather than adding information", on the basis that every tag is classified by hand and an unclassified tag attaches to nothing.
**Measured on the drive, 2026-08-09:**
| tag kind | count |
| --- | --- |
| action | 56 |
| performer-attribute | 13 |
| video-attribute | 3 |
| **unclassified** | **0** |
| **pending tag links** | **0** |
⚠️ **There is no manual work left to remove.** All 72 tags are classified and nothing is waiting on a decision. The report's ranking was correct when written and is not correct now.
⭐ So the value is entirely **future** tags — real, but prospective, and it should be scheduled as such rather than as a backlog-clearing win.
## D1 — What the mapping is, and why it must be proven
```javascript
source:  PEOPLE   SCENE              ACTION
ours:    performer-attribute / video-attribute / action
```
⭐ It looks near-exact. ⚠️ **It must be verified against real tags before anything is auto-classified**, and the ecosystem survey found a specific reason for doubt: the reference consumer fetches `category { id name description }` and **not** `category { group }`. Nobody else relies on the enum, so its population rate is unestablished.
🔴 **Sample before adopting.** One call to `queryTagCategories` takes no arguments and returns the whole taxonomy — enough to check coverage against our 72 tags before a line of mapping code is written.
## 🔴 D2 — Additive only. A classified tag is never reclassified from outside
The rule `GraphSync` already applies to `tagKind`. An operator's classification is a statement; the source's is evidence, and evidence does not overwrite a statement — the same separation `rating` and `preferenceScore` keep, and that `Asset.notes` keeps from a source description.
⚠️ Consequence: on this library the feature would change **nothing at all today**, because all 72 are already classified. That is the correct behaviour and it will look like the feature is broken. Say so in the UI.
## D3 — Aliases feed Repair Tag Spelling, they do not rename anything
The cleanup tool works only from what the library contains, so it can find `Scuba`/`scuba` but not that the source considers a third spelling the same tag.
⚠️ An alias is a **candidate for the existing review**, never an automatic rename. Renaming a tag rewrites every video carrying it.
## D4 — Descriptions: the same rule as scene descriptions
`Tag.description` and `TagCategory.description` are available and unrequested. 🔴 They land in a **source-attributed field**, never over anything the operator wrote — identical reasoning to *Source Descriptions*, and the two should use the same shape so there is one pattern rather than two.
## Test strategy
- **G1** — A tag the operator classified is never reclassified by the source.
- **G2** — An unclassified tag with a confident source category is offered, not applied.
- **G3** — A source category outside the known three is reported, not guessed at.
- **G4** — An alias is offered to Repair Tag Spelling and never renames on its own.
- **G5** — A tag description never overwrites operator text.
## ❓ Open — Human Operator
1. Given zero unclassified tags, is this worth building now, or parked until the vocabulary grows? **Recommend: park, and sample the taxonomy meanwhile** — the sample is one call and it is what tells us whether the mapping holds at all.
2. Should an imported provider vocabulary (the "ten thousand long" case the tag-card design already anticipates) arrive pre-classified? That is what would make this valuable, and it is a different feature.
